name: Bilateral Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnostic Criteria for Bilateral MCDK

criteria.description: Presence of multiple non-communicating cysts of varying sizes replacing normal renal parenchyma on imaging
Involvement of both kidneys with multicystic dysplastic changes
Demonstration of absent or severely reduced renal function bilaterally by radionuclide renal scan or functional imaging
Exclusion of other cystic kidney diseases such as autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) or obstructive cystic dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral multicystic kidneys with absent or severely reduced renal function confirmed by imaging studies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal ultrasound and postnatal imaging are critical for diagnosis; genetic testing may be used to exclude other cystic kidney diseases.

pathognomonic.notes: Due to impaired fetal urine production
searchTerms: very low amniotic fluid before birth
underdeveloped lungs due to low amniotic fluid
abnormal blood minerals like high potassium and acid buildup

occasional.symptomName: Anuria or oliguria in neonatal period
searchTerms: no or very low urine output in newborn
fluid retention due to renal problems

occasional.symptomName: Secondary anemia due to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: anemia caused by chronic kidney disease
low red blood cells from kidney issues

rare.symptomName: Congenital heart defects associated with Potter sequence
searchTerms: heart defects present with Potter sequence
congenital heart abnormalities linked to low amniotic fluid
nerve issues caused by kidney toxins

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal failure
Electrolyte disturbances including hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis
Anemia secondary to chronic kidney disease
imaging: Ultrasound showing multiple non-communicating cysts replacing renal parenchyma bilaterally
Absent or severely reduced renal function on radionuclide renal scan
other: Clinical features of Potter sequence due to oligohydramnios
Pulmonary hypoplasia secondary to decreased amniotic fluid

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse microcystic dilation of collecting ducts
Genetic testing positive for PKHD1 mutations
Cystic changes secondary to urinary tract obstruction
Unilateral or bilateral involvement with evidence of obstruction

redFlags: Severe oligohydramnios leading to pulmonary hypoplasia
Anuria or severe oliguria in neonatal period
Rapid progression to end-stage renal disease in infancy
